column2: follow-up question (asked when this keyPoint is uncertain; must not contain the answer)
How can a society show strength without fighting, by the way it handles hardship and its traditions?
Why does a community that resists a threat for many years need more than a good leader and a cause?
What drew invaders to the subcontinent's plains in the early medieval period, and who attacked first by sea and land?
Which queen defeated a Turkish ruler near Mount Abu in 1178, and which regions escaped Turkic control?
What was the Sultanate's revenue-assignment system and what did it mean for peasants?
Beyond losing territory, what else did kingdoms and chieftains fight to protect when they resisted the Sultanate?
Why did some Rajput kingdoms resist the Mughals while others negotiated, and what did the Mughals want from them?
How did a smaller force use hills and surprise attacks against a mighty empire, and what did Mewar finally gain?
What advantage did Ahom commanders have over invading armies in Assam's landscape?
Which battle in 1671 checked Mughal ambitions in Assam, who led it, and what helped the Ahom navy?
Why was Vijayanagara founded and what made its site so defensible?
What was the empire known for at its height, and what led to its fall?
What does 'swarājya' mean, who championed it among the Marathas, and what did the long wars do to the Mughal Empire?
Why were forts so valuable to the Marathas in a land of hills and valleys, and what else did they do besides defend?
What did the first Sikh Guru teach, and how did the Mughal treatment of the Gurus change the community's outlook?
What were the Akāl Takht, mīrī-pīrī, the Khalsa and the misals, and how did they join faith with self-defence?
Which grievances, economic and religious, pushed the farming Jat community to revolt?
When did the Jat revolts happen, why did the second one come when it did, and was resistance ended by the end of that century?
What were the main features of Bhakti, and how did it spread across the subcontinent?
How could devotion continue when places of worship were closed or destroyed, and how did community singing become a form of protest?
How did writing sacred stories in the languages people spoke and welcoming women devotees build a sense of belonging?
Besides prayer, what did temples do for the economy, for rulers and for the arts?
How did communities protect their sacred places despite destruction, both by repairing and by changing how temples were built?
What was the state's main income, how heavy did it become at times, and what technology helped farmers produce more?
How could a merchant pay a faraway supplier without carrying bags of coins in this period?
How did goods move across the subcontinent and over the sea, and who connected villages with cities?
What roles did merchants play beyond buying and selling, and how did economic strength help communities resist threats?
